lede: Gold fell about 3.6% on Friday to near $3,876, its lowest level in a year, as bets on a December Fed hike and a tech-led stock selloff forced investors to sell. Forex and gold are closed until Monday; crypto stays under pressure after the Binance hack.

focus.text: Broke below $4,000 and closed the week down about 3.7%. It sits under Monday's pivot of 3,924.5; Friday's low near 3,870 is the nearest reference.
Ended October more than 1% lower, near its weakest in over a year, on French fiscal worries and weak growth. Eurozone CPI on Wednesday and US payrolls on Friday are the key tests.

technicals.note: Lower highs and lower lows since the August peak near $4,700. Price is now testing the 3,850–3,880 support zone.

technicals.indicators: Short-term neutral after the rebound from 1.1103
technicals.note: The larger decline from 1.2081 stays in place while 1.1269 holds; a break below 1.1100 would extend it toward the 61.8% retracement.

technicals.indicators: Daily RSI in the mid-30s, near oversold
technicals.note: Testing the 200-day moving average zone after the Binance hack; momentum favours sellers and there is no confirmed reversal signal yet.

technicals.indicators: RSI near the bottom of its neutral range
technicals.note: Fell on heavy volume; holding the 2,170–2,200 area is the first test.

news.text: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% this week but two members voted for a hike; futures now price roughly a 76–80% chance of a December increase.
Gold is now about 27% below its January record. Most Wall Street analysts in Kitco's weekly survey expect further losses; retail voters stay mostly bullish.
The Nasdaq lost 2.9% on Friday as Intel plunged about 29% on weak guidance, deepening doubts about returns on AI spending.
Brent climbed above $113 after a tanker was struck by limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to inflation concerns.
Sterling is near its strongest since mid-September as markets almost fully price a Bank of England hike on 5 November.
Binance lost about $6.3B on 29 Oct in an attack linked to North Korea's TraderTraitor group; roughly $3B has been frozen.
The exchange set aside $6.34B to cover users, aims to reopen withdrawals in phases from Sunday and publish proof of reserves on Monday.
US spot bitcoin ETFs saw $643M of net outflows on Friday, the largest since June, led by BlackRock IBIT and Fidelity FBTC.
Ether, Solana and XRP fell 17–26% in October as the total crypto market value dropped about $360B to $2.58T.
Hyperliquid (+17.7%), Zcash and Monero were the week's top gainers while most large coins declined; BNB held up better than BTC and ETH.

upcoming.event: US clocks go back one hour
upcoming.note: US data now comes one hour later in Turkey time (e.g. payrolls at 16:30).
About 79% priced for a 25bp hike to 4.85%.
All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats; results overnight into Wednesday.
